extracted.intended_audience: Journalists (print, broadcast, digital) transitioning to public relations; social media/digital marketing professionals exploring PR; journalism/communications/PR students; business or corporate writers
extracted.subtask_description: An on-demand certificate program teaching journalists and related professionals how to adapt journalism skills for public relations and communications roles, covering PR strategy, press kits, media relations, PR campaign planning, ethics, and career preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand public relations strategies and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectively understand public relations strategies and effective ways to use public relations to further objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program provides an overview of how PR can be used to further objectives and how participants can apply PR strategies in practice (overall program goal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a public relations campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a public relations campaign and the key elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module content includes an overview of the process of developing a PR campaign and each element within a campaign: research, strategy, messaging, PR tactics and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand media relations from the PR perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand (from the PR perspective) media relations including the development of all the written materials used in this key PR tactic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers press kit components, media outreach best practices, and how PR practitioners develop materials differently than journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position journalistic skills to secure PR roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Position their skills and expertise effectively to help them secure public relations positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program includes practical guidance on discussing and translating journalism experience to appeal to agency and corporate PR recruiters (Module 5, recruiter input).

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand differences in goals between journalism and PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand how the goals of journalism and (journalists) differ from the goals of those working in public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 1 provides an overview of the program and explains how journalists' goals (news gathering, independence) contrast with PR goals (advancing organizational objectives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify transferable journalism skills for PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify how their journalism skills can help them transition into a successful public relations career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 1 highlights specific journalism skills that map to PR functions and how to adapt those skills for PR roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grasp ethical differences and similarities about truth-telling
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn the ethical differences and similarities between journalism and public relations, as related to what constitutes telling the truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 1 emphasizes ethical considerations required by PR professionals and how those compare to journalistic ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand PR's role within integrated communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the intersections (similarities, differences) of public relations with other elements of integrated communications including marketing and advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 2 introduces the breadth of the PR discipline and its position within integrated marketing communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the process and elements of PR planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Get an overview of the process of developing a PR campaign and of each element within a PR campaign including research, strategy, messaging, PR tactics and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 2 breaks down each element of PR planning so participants can identify what goes into campaign development and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the role of social media and content creation in PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn about the role of social media and content creation in PR programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 2 covers how content and social channels integrate into PR tactics and campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know press kit components and have practical templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the knowledge as well as the practical tools and templates for writing essential components of a press kit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 3 lists key press kit elements — news releases, media advisories, fact sheets, backgrounders, Q&As and bios — and provides templates and hands-on tools for writing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand uses and roles of each press kit element
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the uses and roles of the press kit and of each element in communicating a client’s or organization’s message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 3 explains how different press kit pieces function in media outreach and message delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR writing skills beyond news releases (speechwriting, editorials/op-eds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn other PR writing focuses including speechwriting and writing editorials and opinion pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 3 extends PR writing instruction to speechwriting and editorial/op-ed composition as additional tools for influencing audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a news angle to pitch stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how to develop a news angle to successfully pitch a story to the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 4 covers how to identify and craft a newsworthy angle that resonates with journalists and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build relationships with targeted media and create media lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand how to develop relationships with targeted media and build media lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 4 teaches relationship-building techniques and practical steps for assembling and maintaining targeted media lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be familiar with PR distribution services and journalist databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Become familiar with public relations service providers that distribute press materials and offer databases of journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 4 introduces third-party services and subscription tools commonly used to distribute materials and identify media contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master pitching journalists across channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Master the art of pitching journalists by phone, email or social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 4 includes tactics and best practices for pitching via multiple channels and tailoring outreach to the medium and recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand breadth of PR career options and settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the breadth of career options open to them in the PR sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 5 explains agency vs. in-house roles, nonprofit, NGO and government opportunities, and different PR functions (internal/external, public affairs, content creation, digital media).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use subject-matter expertise to obtain PR roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Receive practical knowledge of how to use their skills as subject matter experts to land a PR job.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 5 provides concrete advice on positioning domain expertise and storytelling background to recruiters and hiring managers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for PR job interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Gain insight on how to interview for a PR job.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 5 includes recruiter perspectives and interview best practices tailored to candidates coming from journalism backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know common PR functions and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn about the various PR functions (including internal and external PR, public affairs, content creation, digital media) managed by PR pros in organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 5 maps typical PR responsibilities across organizational types so participants can identify suitable roles.
